searchText: btw maybe Im asking in the wrong place but given the last twitter thread by <@552133098075193354> Is it correct to say that 3074 will be part of Shanghai which will happen in parallel with the Merge (either before or after)? https://twitter.com/nethermindeth/status/1385699335355125766?s=21 Actually this tweet confirms it 😅 Btw, will this merge require running eth2 node in parallel with eth1 node? Are there any resources/documentation on this? I agree, and, the lack of cross-L2 transfers is a bit of a UX nightmare. Not enough to not use L2, but annoying enough. I did see a proposal for cross-L2, if that can become a thing, it’ll be helpful. The rayonism / catalyst docs. In essence yes. You’ll have an application client running the EVM, what is eth1 today, and you’ll have a beacon client handling consensus, as it does now on the beacon chain. Connected via a variant of today’s connection. As I understand it So the docs would be “every eth2 staking setup in existence”, if you want to go high level, just with updated versions of the software, and possibly wss:// instead of http:// or ws:// for the connection mechanism. Or whatever devs decide is the right transport. Oof. Running two nodes at once... That would be a UX nightmare We still have an audit of the spec in progress and that will better inform the decision. I think it's understood community *wants* it or something like it, it's just a matter of ensuring it is done safely. Yes. You will need an execution client and a consensus client. Is there any certain reason behind doing the merge? I mean, eth1 network currently works without issues on POW And no additional setup pain is required Just to run geth and that's it We can't get off of POW without getting off of POW 🤣 . Ethereum is switching to POS. There *could* be a temporary reduction in UX having to run two clients but this will almost definitely be ironed out back into a smooth user experience. I mean, how switching to PoS will help eth1? For eth2 it is essential Because it does't work in another way I'd recommend going and reading some of the previously published materials about scaling via sharding and how that plays into Eth1/Eth2 and the merge. This? https://ethereum.org/en/eth2/docking/ > I mean, how switching to PoS will help eth1? The ecosystem no longer burning >$1.5B per month on computing+hardware resource expenditure, essentially gotcha Though, it is a tradeoff Either UX either POS (on eth1) I think PoS will actually have better UX Here's a few examples: I mean in the sense that users will be required to run two nodes Instead of only one * Blocks come every 12 seconds, instead of a Poisson distribution, which means that on average users need to wait 6 seconds and they'll never need to wait more than 12 for a block, whereas today users sometimes need to wait a long time * >100 confirmations per block, so you get security faster * Casper FFG finality * Much better light client experience Oh I agree this is a problem, though imo it should not be hard to solve Ideally one node would just turn the other node on automatically But still, two separate processes Two epochs to finalize? Does that matter? If geth had ten processes internally all along, would you notice? Right, though the probability of reversion is tiny even before then Yes. It is convenient to see only one process in `htop` or anything like this And in some other cases too Though yes, it is not a huge problem isn't it relatively simple to bundle two clients into one? Well, in theory you can pack them into one binary But they will be separate in any case separate in terms of development? FYI, many exchanges do not require more than 15 blocks to confirm transactions. 15*13/60 = 3.25 minutes compared with 2 epoch's 12 minutes <tkstanczak> Separate as processes and modules. So PoW can be actually faster at this point PoS gives the same level of security as 15 PoW confirmations in like 3 confirmations Correct me if I'm wrong <tkstanczak> Generally more modular architecture is safer. Eth2 node could always fallback to backup eth1 node process if primary fails. do you think people will run more than one eth1 node process? Yes, but full finality on beacon chain is achieved in two epochs correct whereas in PoW full finality is never achieved In theory that can be fixed actually it can't Depends on how easy it will be And that's inherent to the "anonymous" and registration-free nature of PoW True though So the entire discussion can be summarized as "Does getting rid of miner block rewards worth making the Ethereum UX worse?" I still don't think the UX will become worse But I know that's not up to me to just assert Hopefully we'll see at or soon after the end of rayonism some practical demos of what a two-client architecture would look like I expect it will be a single button push or command line to turn on a node Yea, but still, what if one of the nodes will be down? Then the other node will restart it? for example: eth1 or eth2 node is having troubles finding peers behind NAT Oh, so post-merge if the execution layer (eth1) node has a p2p failure that should only affect the txpool, it would not affect other functionality Behind NAT geth is having hard times finding peers eth2 nodes might as well I definitely expect that the p2p layers will become unified fairly soon after the merge So there isn't a double-risk of something breaking Well, this is only one example In reality there are a ton of them Just can't remember all I think my core point is that there is not _that_ large a difference between two pieces of software talking to each other via RPC and two pieces of software where one accesses the other via library calls It would be nice if a research would have been done about this Before the eth1 merge actually happens I expect that's part of what the rayonism project going on right now is all about! So we will know how it will affect UX Oh cool Was not aware of it https://rayonism.io/ Thanks for flagging all these issues btw; it's definitely important for us to make sure we think about the issues and actually implement the things that need to be implemented to make the post-merge experience seamless 👍 it doesn't seem that UX is within the scope of rayonism currently Makes sense; first step is to get it working at all, second step is to polish it But even still, the first step will make it clear to all the devs what needs to be polished IMHO it is better to make the merge after Ethereum network really requires it Aka after the phase 1 Or later, don't know in detail what different phases on eth2 do Let me rephrase it: to make the merge after eth2 is done This is the most seamless way of moving Ethereum to POS Though, it will cost some money As miner block rewards eth2 isn't done without the merge the UX is definitely affected on an explorer level 😆 Don't think it matters much for people who run nodes. The problem is that it actually takes extra effort to make sharding actually useful if the merge is not yet done hahaha What are the plans for re-merging etherchain and beaconcha.in (and I guess I could ask the same question to etherscan and beaconscan) after the merge btw? Is there a plan for that? Yep, this is the tradeoff still unclear since there's still time - as for testnets, the scale is not too big, so it will just be on beaconcha.in. For the mainnet we definitely don't want users to hop between two explorers (etherchain for pre merge tx, beaconcha.in for post merge). We may mirror the same data on beaconcha.in<>beaconcha.in for a while. I hope we can get a fully working eth1 & eth2 explorer open source the tricky part is sharding beaconcha.in itself is not only an explorer but also has become a validator monitoring tool 😻 goodjob 3074 has not been accepted formally yet FYI, there still is a pending audit Holding my eth and honestly a little excited to see what deflation has on eth values and supply post 1559. Going to be a very interesting economics and financial experiment. PS: Already interesting to see eth vs eth2 staked tokens with a 1-0.91 ratio on binance. i'd take this with a grain of salt, Tomasz seems more optimistic than the other client teams 😃 <tkstanczak> I was to ask, what other teams are saying? <tkstanczak> I think I took that October thing from Dankrad <tkstanczak> would be good to hear from Peter <dankrad> There are some strong internal reasons to work for an October deadline <dankrad> But yes we should see what the teams say internal reasons? <dankrad> yes :) <dankrad> there are also very good external reasons though <dankrad> each month corresponds to over 370k new ETH issued <dankrad> and more than one megaton of CO2 <dankrad> so I think being ambitious here is imperative <tkstanczak> I mean, we probably can handle October if my intuition about complexity of delivery is right but the testing will probably take long time. I think that targeting October may mean the final spec and working testnet but then we want proper time before the actual switch. <tkstanczak> Also eth2 teams were not widely represented on the ACD when we mentioned October. There was Danny, I think and maybe one more person from eth2. <dankrad> I think the changes required on the Eth2 client side are extremely simple <tkstanczak> It may be that the eth2 change complexity will be higher than that on the eth1 side? <dankrad> Eth2 clients should most definitely not be what holds the merge back <tkstanczak> Ok, that was my intuition for eth2 but then I started thinking that maybe I am totally wrong. <tkstanczak> I would listen to Peter - he will have a very reasonable and slightly more conservative estimate. <tkstanczak> Together with Martin they can measure the impl + testing effort. <tkstanczak> We will for sure put a lot of resources to getting it done. <dankrad> I will invite Greta on the call as well <dankrad> she may have some opinions on helping conserve something else :) <tkstanczak> Oh, I have to admit that this is not what I am taking into account... <dankrad> (to be clear, I will not seriously do this. I just want to point out that there are serious externalities that are not reflected in how difficult we find it from a technical viewpoint) <tkstanczak> I mean externalities are just this, they will not make us move faster or slower. <tkstanczak> What I care about is the ability to deliver with good qualoty and safety <dankrad> But there is always prioritization <tkstanczak> Where do you think community stands? <tkstanczak> I would not make too many assumptions. <dankrad> and "good quality and safety" is not some absolute measure. I generally agree that these are also important, but it's overall a multidimensional optimization problem and none of these are absolute <tkstanczak> Not a homogenous group. <dankrad> I think the community wants a merge very soon <dankrad> of courser there are safety and quality concerns <dankrad> BUT we should not pretend that the status quo is perfectly safe! <dankrad> It is extremely vulnerable to miner attacks who see their fortunes dwindling as we speak <tkstanczak> Oh community wants everything very soon but they prioritize. And they definitely have different views depending on the projects they work on. <tkstanczak> I keep saying that miners are really fantastic and part of the good things... (re @dankrad: It is extremely vulnerable to miner attacks who see their fortunes dwindling as we speak) <tkstanczak> Same if miners would say that core devs can attack... we are working on it together. <dankrad> I mean there have been some serious threats recently <dankrad> mining is also not very decentralized <tkstanczak> They were so not serious that I ignored them knowing they were not. You mean 1st of April? <dankrad> no <tkstanczak> PoS is capital based, why it would be less centralized? Do we have the expectatiom of PoS being less centralized? <dankrad> yes <tkstanczak> I trust Vitalik and researchers here but my personal intuition is that PoS is a failure in the long ter
